title: Waves, Interference and Optics
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Physics: Waves and Optics Worksheets
standard_text: Progressive and stationary waves, the wave equation, phase difference, refraction and refractive index, total internal reflection and optical fibres, interference and Young's double-slit experiment, diffraction and the diffraction grating.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level physics worksheets on waves: v = fλ, phase difference, stationary waves, refraction and critical angles, Young's double slits and diffraction gratings. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: v = fλ; dsinθ = nλ; w = λD/s.
key_sub: Path difference of a whole number of wavelengths gives a maximum.
body_html:
How to think about it

For any wave v = fλ and f = 1/T. A stationary wave on a string fixed at both ends has λ = 2L/n. Light slows in glass: n = c/v, and n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Total internal reflection happens beyond the critical angle, sin C = n₂/n₁.

Coherent sources interfere: a path difference of nλ gives a bright fringe. Young's slits: w = λD/s. A grating: d sin θ = nλ.

Example

Grating with 300 lines per mm, λ = 600 nm. Angle of first order?

d = 3.33 × 10−6 m

sin θ = 0.18

Answer: 10.4°

Example

Critical angle for glass, n = 1.50?

sin C = 1/1.50

Answer: 41.8°

Common mistakes

  • Using lines per mm as d without taking 1/N.
  • Leaving the slit separation in mm.
  • Using λ = L (not 2L) for the fundamental.

faq.q: What is the diffraction grating equation?
faq.a: d sin θ = nλ, where d is the slit spacing (1 ÷ lines per metre) and n is the order.

faq.q: When does total internal reflection happen?
faq.a: When light goes into a medium with a lower refractive index and the angle of incidence is bigger than the critical angle.
